In contrast, white-box testing methods, leveraging the underlying mechanics of GCNs, can be more efficient but are hindered by the lack of suitable testing methods. Existing work primarily focuses on evaluating the performance of GCNs using classification metrics, neglecting to explore their robustness against perturbations in input data, which is a critical aspect of their behavior. To address this limitation, we introduce GraphMask, a white-box, white-field testing framework designed to assess the robustness of GCNs under random node mask perturbations. This framework enables the evaluation of GCNs' robustness in a controlled, automated, and efficient manner. Experimental results demonstrate GraphMask's effectiveness in uncovering both common and complex issues in GCNs, underscoring its utility in ensuring the robustness of models prior to their deployment in high-stakes environments.
